newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC seen opting for lower maize export figures.
newsitem.headline: ONIC seen opting for lower maize export figures.

text.p: French cereals authority ONIC has narrowed its estimates for maize exports and stocks this season to show exports at the bottom end of previous forecasts, grain industry sources said on Tuesday.
A draft ONIC report prepared for publication next Wednesday suggests France will export 250,000 tonnes of maize to non-EU countries in the year to June 30, 1997, they said.
This compares with a wide range of estimates in a previous monthly report, published ahead of the harvest, that showed exports anywhere between 250,000 and 1.25 million tonnes.
For projected carryover stocks at the season's close, ONIC settled on a figure near the top end of its previous range at a little over 2.7 million tonnes, the industry sources said.
ONIC last month projected a 1996/97 carryover stock of between two and three million tonnes.
The decisions were taken at a private meeting of ONIC industry advisers in Paris on Tuesday but can be adjusted by a full panel of ONIC members before publication on November 13.
The panel recommended little change in ONIC's 1996 maize crop forecast of 13.6 million tonnes or in its target for maize exports within the EU of 5.6 million tonnes.
In 1995/96, France exported 164,000 tonnes of maize outside the EU and 6.087 million tonnes inside the 15-nation area from a harvest of 12.394 million tonnes.
Its closing maize stocks on June 30 this year were 1.653 million tonnes.
